title: Standardize correlation IDs (request_id, trace_id, admin_action_id) in audit events across services
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Problem
Today, audit events are emitted by multiple producers (API Gateway, Control Plane, Console backend, policy engine, Private installer) with inconsistent correlation identifiers. During investigations (support escalations, SOC2 evidence pulls, customer SIEM triage), we frequently cannot reliably link:
- a user/admin action (Console click or API call)
- the originating HTTP request(s)
- downstream service calls / async tasks
- the resulting audit event(s)

This ticket standardizes correlation IDs across services and ensures audit events include stable, consistent fields: request_id, trace_id, and admin_action_id.

Goals
- Make it possible to follow a sensitive action end-to-end from edge -> internal services -> audit log -> SIEM.
- Ensure Hosted/Dedicated/Private parity (same semantics/fields).
- Avoid high cardinality / PII issues (IDs are opaque; do not include user-provided input).

Non-goals
- Changing audit event taxonomy or adding new sensitive-action coverage (tracked in other tickets).
- Enforcing a single tracing vendor; we’ll follow W3C trace context conventions and OpenTelemetry propagation.

Definitions / Field semantics (v1)
1) request_id
- What: unique per inbound HTTP request at the edge (API Gateway / Console backend edge).
- Format: ULID (preferred) or UUIDv4 (acceptable during transition). Must be opaque, lower-case.
- Propagation: via header `x-redwood-request-id` (internal) and `x-request-id` (external/backcompat). When both exist, prefer `x-redwood-request-id`.
- Logging: included in all audit events where an HTTP request exists.

2) trace_id
- What: distributed trace identifier for the request across services.
- Format: 16-byte hex string from W3C trace context (OpenTelemetry `trace_id`), 32 lowercase hex chars.
- Propagation: W3C `traceparent` header for HTTP; gRPC metadata equivalent; for async jobs propagate explicitly via job payload context.
- Logging: included in all audit events where tracing is available; if not available, omit (do not synthesize).

3) admin_action_id
- What: stable identifier for a user-initiated admin workflow that may span multiple HTTP requests and/or async operations (e.g., “Update RBAC role”, “Rotate API key”, “Change export destination”, “Apply Private config”).
- Format: ULID.
- Creation:
  - Console: generated client-side at action start OR server-side at first admin mutation endpoint; persisted through subsequent calls.
  - API: generated server-side for admin endpoints if not provided.
- Propagation: header `x-redwood-admin-action-id` between Console <-> backend; internal propagation via request context.
- Logging: included in audit events for sensitive actions initiated by Console/admin flows; optional for purely system-initiated events.

Implementation plan
A) Standard library + middleware
- Add `correlation` helpers to the shared audit event library to:
  - parse inbound headers (`x-redwood-request-id`, `x-request-id`, `traceparent`, `x-redwood-admin-action-id`)
  - generate missing request_id/admin_action_id where appropriate
  - attach correlation to request context and downstream clients
- Standardize field names in audit events:
  - `request_id`
  - `trace_id`
  - `admin_action_id`

B) Edge behavior
- API Gateway:
  - Ensure every inbound request has a request_id (generate if absent).
  - Ensure trace context is established (OTel) and propagated downstream.
  - Include request_id/trace_id on all audit events emitted by the gateway.
- Console backend:
  - Accept/propagate admin_action_id.
  - For multi-step workflows, ensure the same admin_action_id is used across each audited mutation.

C) Downstream services
- Control plane + policy engine:
  - Update client wrappers to forward correlation headers.
  - Update audit emission to read correlation from context.

D) Async/background tasks
- Where an audited action is executed asynchronously (e.g., policy compilation job, export target validation job):
  - store correlation fields in the job payload (explicit allow-list)
  - restore to context before emitting audit events

Acceptance criteria
- For a representative set of sensitive actions (RBAC change, API key rotate, export config change, policy update):
  - Audit event contains request_id
  - Audit event contains trace_id when trace context exists
  - Audit event contains admin_action_id for Console-initiated actions
- request_id is stable from edge -> downstream and appears consistently in logs/traces and audit events.
- Backcompat:
  - If only `x-request-id` exists, it is mapped into request_id.
  - No breaking change for existing clients; new header names are additive.
- Documentation:
  - Update engineering standard to include header/field names + generation rules.

Risks / Notes
- Cardinality: correlation IDs are expected to be high-cardinality but are necessary for investigations; limit their use to correlation fields only (do not include in dimensions for metrics aggregation except sampled debugging metrics).
- Duplicates: request_id/admin_action_id are not idempotency keys. SIEM de-dupe must rely on event_id (separate guidance).
- Private deployments: if tracing is not enabled in some customer environments, trace_id may be absent; request_id/admin_action_id must still work.

Rollout
- Phase 1: Gateway + shared library + control plane propagation
- Phase 2: Console admin_action_id support
- Phase 3: Async propagation for known job queues used by audited actions

Test plan
- Unit tests for header parsing and precedence rules.
- Integration tests (E2E) assert correlation fields present and consistent across emitted audit events for the selected sensitive actions.

References
- GitHub PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-22047-audit-event-correlation-request-id-trace-id.json
- Related tickets: ENG-4821 (schema v1), ENG-4827 (exporter tagging/normalization), ENG-4834 (E2E tests)
- Motivation: support escalations where we couldn’t correlate missing events in Private to the initiating admin workflow (see SUP-18421 context via escalation thread)
activity: 2026-01-15 Allison Grant created ticket after schema workshop feedback that investigations were blocked by missing/ambiguous request IDs.
2026-01-22 Caleb Johnson aligned on W3C trace context + OTel as the trace_id source; agreed not to synthesize trace_id when absent.
2026-01-28 Ethan Park confirmed control plane services can forward `x-redwood-request-id` and `traceparent` through existing HTTP client wrappers.
2026-02-03 Nadia Rahman requested explicit precedence rules: prefer x-redwood-request-id over x-request-id; do not overwrite if present.
2026-02-07 Chloe Martin flagged Console workflows that span multiple endpoints; proposal: admin_action_id created at first mutation and echoed back to client.
2026-02-12 PR opened to implement correlation propagation + audit emission fields; added basic unit tests for parsing/format validation.
2026-02-18 PR merged; follow-up note to ensure E2E tests assert admin_action_id for Console-initiated sensitive actions.
comments: Marcus Lin (2026-01-23): Please make sure admin_action_id semantics are clear for Private installer actions too. Even if there is no browser, we should allow operator tools to pass a stable ID across an install/upgrade step chain.

Logan Wright (2026-01-30): For coverage dashboard, request_id is the join key between audit events and ingress logs. We should keep the header name stable and ensure it’s present even if tracing is disabled.
Kevin Osei (2026-02-05): Exporter should treat correlation fields as pass-through and never mutate them. Normalization should only map legacy `requestId`/`traceId` producers into the v1 field names.

Sean Gallagher (2026-02-08): Be careful not to fail admin endpoints if headers are malformed. Parse best-effort; if invalid, generate new request_id and omit invalid traceparent rather than rejecting.
Allison Grant (2026-02-19): Once this lands, please update the audit logging standard doc to explicitly list the header names and field names so service owners don’t invent new variants.
